models_evaluated: EHR-based CRE risk prediction model (Chicago CDC Prevention Epicenters model optimized for Emory Healthcare)

links.outcome: Prospective discrimination on live EHR data versus derivation cohort
links.effect: AUC 0.66 prospectively vs 0.73 (95% CI 0.60–0.87) in derivation cohort; authors describe it as comparable, with moderate discrimination.
links.quote: The model demonstrated moderate discriminative performance (AUC of 0.66) under real-world conditions, comparable to that in the original derivation cohort (AUC, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.60–0.87).

openai.sample_unit: screened admission encounters, including repeat admissions
models_evaluated: EHR-integrated CRE risk prediction model developed by Chicago CDC Prevention Epicenters and optimized for Emory Healthcare

links.outcome: Screening yield and carrier detection when testing only a high-risk subset
links.effect: At ≥0.16%, 58 (17%) met testing criteria and 6 (10%) were CRE-positive, versus 11 (3.2%) among all 342 screened encounters. Sensitivity was 55%.
links.quote: Based on the sample of patients we tested, 58 (17%) met this threshold for testing (ie, they had CRE risk score ≥0.16%) and 6 (10%) of those that met the threshold were positive for CRE (Table 4 ).

links.outcome: Screening workload and diagnostic performance across alternative risk thresholds
links.effect: Raising the threshold from 0.16% to 0.36% reduced screening from 20 to 5 patients/week; PPV increased from 10.3% to 18.8%, while sensitivity decreased from 54.5% to 27.3%.
links.quote: For example, using a higher cutoff (≥0.36%) may be more practical as it would require screening fewer patients (∼5/week) with a higher PPV (19%), while only sacrificing a small decrease in NPV (98.2% to 97.5%).

links.effect: At the optimal testing threshold of 0.16%, the screening program cost $8,015 monthly, potentially cost-effective if it prevented one CRE infection every three months.
links.quote: Using $30,484 as the estimated cost of a healthcare-associated infection with CRE, this screening program could be cost-effective if it prevented at least one healthcare-associated CRE infection every three months.

links.effect: Running the model prospectively on live production data in silent mode yielded an AUC of 0.66.
links.quote: The AUC of the model incorporated into the EHR report was 0.66

links.effect: Raising the threshold to 0.36% would reduce screening volume to 5 patients per week and increase PPV to 19%, while minimally reducing NPV.
links.quote: For example, using a higher cutoff (≥0.36%) may be more practical as it would require screening fewer patients (∼5/week) with a higher PPV (19%), while only sacrificing a small decrease in NPV (98.2% to 97.5%).
